guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not treating Wake Forest’s opener as proof that its offense will travel against a much stronger defense. We saw real positives: Wake Forest generated 559 yards, Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions, and the offensive line did not allow a sack. That performance gives us useful context, but our longer-run numbers still view Miami’s pass defense as a significant step up in class.

What stands out to us is Miami’s ability to limit both passing efficiency and scoring-opportunity creation, the two areas most likely to determine whether Wake Forest can stay within the number. Wake Forest produced two long touchdown passes against Akron, but we do not want to assume that kind of explosiveness is repeatable here. Our view is already closely aligned with the market, so we do not see enough pricing separation to justify a position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, the matchup to watch is Lopez and Wake Forest’s passing game against Miami’s pass defense. We saw Lopez push the ball downfield effectively in his debut, including touchdown completions of 78 and 72 yards, while Wake Forest kept him clean. The question is whether Wake Forest can create sustainable drives when those explosive plays are harder to find.

We think protection is central to that question. If Wake Forest again gives Lopez time, its receivers have shown they can generate chunk gains; if Miami forces the offense to string together shorter plays, our numbers favor the defense’s ability to prevent quality scoring chances.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 356 passing yards and 203 rushing yards.
Wake Forest allowed Akron 305 total yards, including 149 rushing and 156 passing, while recording two sacks and seven tackles for loss.
Wake Forest committed no turnovers and recovered one Akron fumble.

quarterback.fact: North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's starting quarterback and one of six team captains.
In his Wake Forest debut against Akron, Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing seven times for 39 yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of his collegiate career.
Lopez previously played under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell at South Alabama.
The unofficial depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as Lopez's backup.

offensive_personnel.fact: The unofficial offensive line lists Tolu Olajide at left tackle, Clinton Richard at left guard, Will Way at center, Ryan Berger at right guard and Aidan Martin at right tackle.
Center Will Way joined Wake Forest from Weber State in January 2026 and was selected as a team captain.
Wake Forest did not allow a sack in its season opener against Akron.
The unofficial depth chart lists Carlos Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks as the first receivers at the Z, X and H positions, respectively.
Ty Clark III is listed first at running back after rushing seven times for a career-high 105 yards against Akron, including a 57-yard run.
Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron, including a 78-yard touchdown, and added 18 punt-return yards.
Antonio Meeks recorded 93 receiving yards against Akron.

defensive_personnel.fact: The unofficial defensive front lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.

The unofficial depth chart lists Frank Cusano and Aiden Hall at linebacker, Braylon Johnson at star, Deuce Blades II and Ashaad Williams at cornerback, Rushaun Tongue at free safety and Davaughn Patterson at strong safety.
Aiden Hall became a starter in 2025 and finished that season with 73 tackles, eight tackles for loss and three passes defended.
Rushaun Tongue recovered Wake Forest's only forced turnover against Akron.
Against Akron, Vincent Firenze recorded nine tackles and forced a fumble, while Frank Cusano also recorded nine tackles.

coaching_changes.fact: Dyrell Roberts joined Wake Forest as wide receivers coach for the 2026 season after coaching East Carolina's receivers from 2023 through 2025.
Jake Dickert is in his second season as Wake Forest's head coach after leading the team to a 9-4 record and a Duke's Mayo Bowl victory in 2025.
Rob Ezell is Wake Forest's offensive coordinator, Scottie Hazelton is defensive coordinator and Freddie Banks is co-defensive coordinator and safeties coach.

offensive_context.fact: Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs and both of its fourth-down attempts against Akron.
Wake Forest scored on four of five red-zone possessions against Akron.
Wake Forest's season-opening passing attack produced touchdown completions of 78 yards to Carlos Hernandez and 72 yards to Antonio Meeks.

defensive_context.fact: Wake Forest allowed Akron to convert 6 of 14 third downs and score on all three of its red-zone possessions.
Wake Forest forced at least one turnover in 70 of its previous 84 games through the Akron opener.

special_teams.fact: Connor Calvert made three field goals against Akron and scored 12 points.
Freshman Ethan Hyams is listed as the first punter, with Jack Ploszay behind him; Wake Forest recorded a 49.0-yard net punting average against Akron.
The unofficial depth chart lists Koredell Bartley as the primary kickoff returner and Carlos Hernandez as the primary punt returner.

other_relevant.fact: Wake Forest had eight returning starters entering the 2026 season.
